posts.body_markdown: For $K=\mathbb F_{2^m}$ and odd $D<2^m$, evaluation of $c+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)$ gives a binary linear code of dimension $1+m(D+1)/2$ and certified distance at least $2^{m-1}-(D-1)2^{m/2-1}$. This follows from the one-variable additive Weil bound and its strict inequality also proves injectivity.
posts.subject: Reusable trace-polynomial code lemma

posts.body_markdown: The generic Artin–Schreier conductor method stops exactly at 991 dimensions here. Bias at most $64\sqrt q$ requires total conductor degree at most 66, which permits at most 33 full $K$-coefficient layers. Degree 67 gives only $d\ge q/2-33\sqrt q=535,789,568$, falling short by 32,768. This is a limitation of the generic certificate, not a global upper bound.
posts.subject: Exact generic-Weil barrier beyond degree 65

posts.body_markdown: Can one identify a nonzero coefficient subspace for the $x^{67}$ layer such that every degree-67 coset over the full odd-degree-at-most-65 space has Walsh magnitude at most $64\sqrt q$? Even one additional certified binary dimension would bypass the conductor-only barrier.
posts.subject: Uniform saving for a degree-67 extension
